about: Periodic Labs is a Menlo Park, California AI research start-up founded in 2025 by former OpenAI and Google DeepMind researchers Liam Fedus and Ekin Dogus Cubuk, aiming to build AI scientists and automated labs to discover new materials, such as superconductors. It launched with a seed round of about 300 million dollars from investors including a16z, Nvidia and others. It is a B2B deep tech company with a high profile in AI circles, but no consumer products.

Sesame is a San Francisco AI start-up building lifelike conversational voice assistants and smart glasses, known for its Maya and Miles voice demos released in 2025 and its work on natural-sounding speech. Founded by Oculus co-founder Brendan Iribe and Ankit Kumar, it raised a $250 million round in 2025 led by Sequoia and Spark, with total funding of about $308 million. It is a young consumer AI company with a high tech-press profile.

wiki.title: Sesame
wiki.what: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds
wiki.text: Sesame is a plant in the genus Sesamum, also called benne. Numerous wild relatives occur in Africa and a smaller number in India. It is widely naturalized in tropical regions around the world and is cultivated for its edible seeds, which grow in pods. World production in 2024 was 6.7 million tonnes, with India, Myanmar, and Sudan as the largest producers.

about: Soluna Holdings is a Albany, New York company (listed here with a New York base) that builds data centers co-located with renewable energy projects, offering Bitcoin mining hosting and other flexible computing workloads, including AI. It is listed on Nasdaq (SLNH). Customers are crypto miners and AI users. Funding is shown at about $294 million. It is a B2B digital infrastructure business, with little consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Soluna
wiki.text: Soluna was a music group consisting of four members, all of Hispanic descent – Aurora Rodriguez, America Olivo, Jessica Castellanos, and Christina "T" López. The group's name is the combination the Spanish words for sun ("sol") and moon ("luna"). Both Lopez and Castellanos are pursuing primarily solo music careers, and Olivo is developing an acting resume, including a recent role on General Hospital.

about: Certn is a Victoria, British Columbia based Canadian background screening company, offering AI-assisted criminal record checks, identity verification and tenant and employment screening to employers and landlords. Founded in 2017 by Andrew Wlasiuk and others, it is listed as having raised about $253 million, an amount that seems high for its stage. It operates in Canada, the US, the UK and elsewhere. It is a B2B service with limited consumer awareness.

about: Nozomi Networks is a San Francisco cybersecurity company providing visibility, threat detection and monitoring for industrial control systems, operational technology and IoT networks in energy, manufacturing, transport and critical infrastructure. Founded in 2013 in Switzerland, it was acquired by Mitsubishi Electric in 2025 for about 1 billion dollars. It has raised around $266 million. It is a B2B security brand with recognition among OT security buyers and little consumer visibility.

Path Robotics is a Columbus, Ohio company building AI-driven robotic welding systems that sense and adapt to parts without programming, selling to metal fabrication and manufacturing shops. Founded in 2018 by Andrew Lonsberry and Alexander Zak, it has raised about $271 million from investors including Lux Capital and Drive Capital. Customers are industrial manufacturers, mostly in the US. It is a B2B robotics brand with no consumer awareness.

Turing is a San Francisco company that supplies AI training data, evaluation and research services to frontier model labs, plus a talent platform connecting engineers to remote work. Customers include leading AI developers and enterprises building generative AI systems. Founded in 2018 by Jonathan Siddharth and Vijay Krishnan, it was valued at about 2.2 billion dollars in 2025 and has raised roughly $270 million. It is a B2B AI services brand with a notable profile in tech circles.

wiki.title: Alan Turing
wiki.text: Alan Mathison Turing was an English mathematician and logician widely regarded as the father of theoretical computer science. He formalised the concepts of algorithm and computation with the Turing machine, a model of a general-purpose computer, and his contributions to cryptanalysis helped the Allies of World War II decipher messages encrypted by the German Enigma machine. He also contributed the Turing test to philosophy of artificial intelligence and the Turing pattern concept to mathematical and theoretical biology.

about: Aleo is a San Francisco blockchain company building a privacy-focused layer one network that uses zero-knowledge proofs, so developers can build private applications. It launched its mainnet in 2024, and its Leo programming language is used for smart contracts. Founded in 2019, it raised a 200 million dollar Series B in 2022 led by Kora Management, with total funding around $249 million. It is a crypto infrastructure project with a profile in developer and crypto circles, not a consumer brand.

Tietoevry is a Nordic IT services and software company, headquartered in Espoo, Finland (formed in 2019 from the merger of Finnish Tieto and Swedish Evry), offering consulting, cloud, data, software and digital engineering services to banks, governments, healthcare and industry. It has roughly 20,000 employees and revenue of about 3 billion euros, with a listing in Helsinki, Stockholm and Oslo (TIETO). B2B with limited public awareness outside the Nordics.

wiki.title: Tieto
wiki.what: Finnish IT software and service company
wiki.text: Tieto Corporation is a Finnish IT software and service company providing IT and product engineering services. Tieto is domiciled in Espoo, Finland, and the company's shares are listed on the NASDAQ OMX Helsinki, NASDAQ OMX Stockholm and Oslo Stock Exchange. Tieto has approximately 15,000 employees across 20 countries, and has customers in the energy, forestry, banking, healthcare and public sectors.

about: Backblaze is a US cloud storage and backup company based in San Mateo, California, offering B2 cloud storage (an S3-compatible service for businesses) and consumer computer backup, with exabytes of data stored. It earns subscription and usage revenue from consumers, SMEs and media firms, and is known for publishing hard drive failure statistics. Founded in 2007 and listed on Nasdaq (BLZE) since 2021. Well-known among technical users, with moderate consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Backblaze
wiki.text: Backblaze, Inc. is an American cloud storage and data backup company based in San Mateo, California. It was founded in 2007 by Gleb Budman and others. Its services are intended for both business and personal markets.

about: Gravis Robotics is a Swiss robotics company, based in Zurich and spun out of ETH Zurich, developing autonomous technology for heavy construction machines such as excavators, so they can work with little human supervision. Customers are construction and earthmoving firms. It has raised about 223 million dollars per the input, which should be checked. B2B with no consumer awareness.

Izertis is a Spanish technology consulting and digital services company based in Gijon, Asturias, offering software development, cloud, data, AI and cybersecurity services to enterprises and public bodies in Spain, Portugal, the UK, Colombia and Mexico. It grew by acquisition and is listed on BME Growth (Madrid). B2B, with regional awareness in Spain.

Kore.ai is a US enterprise conversational and agentic AI platform company based in Orlando, Florida (the input lists San Mateo, California), selling virtual assistants, contact centre automation and AI agents to banks, retailers, healthcare and other large companies. It has raised over 200 million dollars from investors including FirstMark and Vista. B2B with no consumer awareness.

LawZero is a non-profit AI safety research organisation based in Montreal, launched in 2025 by Turing Award winner Yoshua Bengio, working on safe-by-design AI systems (the Scientist AI concept). It is funded by philanthropic donors and not a commercial firm. High credibility in AI policy, but not a typical commercial sponsorship target.

wiki.title: Yoshua Bengio
wiki.text: Yoshua Bengio is a Canadian computer scientist, and a pioneer of artificial neural networks and deep learning.

about: Matic Robots is a US home robotics company based in Mountain View, California, that makes an autonomous home robot vacuum and mop using vision-only navigation, with no cloud dependence. Founded by former Google X and Tesla engineers, it sells to consumers and has raised about 227 million dollars. Early-stage consumer hardware brand with low awareness.

TRM Labs is a US blockchain intelligence company based in San Francisco that sells software for tracing cryptocurrency transactions, detecting fraud and illicit finance, and supporting compliance and investigations. Customers are law enforcement, tax agencies, banks, crypto exchanges and payment firms in many countries. Founded in 2018, it raised a large 2025 round at a valuation of about 1 billion dollars, with total funding near 220 million dollars. B2B and government-facing, known in crypto and compliance circles, with no consumer brand awareness.

Turing is a Japanese AI start-up based in Tokyo, founded in 2021, that develops AI technology and software aimed at fully autonomous driving, including end-to-end driving models and its own vehicle platform. It sells to car makers and mobility partners and has raised about 244 million dollars in total. Early-stage deep-tech company with little general public awareness, though known within Japan's AI and automotive circles.

about: Blitzy is a US generative AI software development platform based in Boston, Massachusetts, which uses autonomous AI agents to plan and write large amounts of enterprise code for existing codebases. It sells to large software and enterprise engineering teams and has raised about 210 million dollars. Early-stage B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Blitzy
wiki.text: Blitzy is an American artificial intelligence company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, that develops an autonomous software development platform for large enterprises. The company's software reverse-engineers an organization's existing codebase into a knowledge graph and coordinates large numbers of AI agents to modernize legacy software and build new applications, with a human engineer approving and completing the final portion of the work.

about: HappyRobot is a US AI company based in San Francisco that sells AI workers (voice agents) automating phone calls and workflows for logistics and supply chain companies, such as freight brokers and carriers. It has raised about 211 million dollars. Early-stage B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

K1x is a US technology company based in Morristown, New Jersey, which develops AI software for tax compliance and related financial reporting. The input shows funding of about 210 million dollars. Customers and scale are not described in the input. Early-stage B2B with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Netomi is a US customer service AI company based in San Mateo, California that sells AI agents and automation for email, chat, voice and messaging support, used by e-commerce, travel and retail brands. Founded in 2015, it has raised about 217 million dollars. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Netomi
wiki.text: Netomi, formerly msg.ai, is an American artificial intelligence company and developer of chatbot technologies.

about: Obsidian Security is a US cybersecurity company based in Palo Alto, California that sells software for securing SaaS applications and AI agents, with threat detection, posture management and identity security. Customers include large enterprises, and it has raised about 205 million dollars. B2B with brand awareness among security teams and none among consumers.

Savvy Wealth is a US technology-enabled wealth management firm based in New York that combines human financial advisers with AI and software to serve affluent clients. It is backed by investors including Y Combinator-linked and other funds and has raised about 206 million dollars. Early-stage consumer finance brand with limited awareness.

Silk is a US software company based in Needham, Massachusetts that provides software-defined cloud storage for databases and enterprise workloads, running on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud and speeding up block storage. It was previously called Kaminario and has raised about 211 million dollars. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Silk
wiki.what: Fine, lustrous, natural fiber produced by various arthropods
wiki.text: Silk is a natural protein fiber, some forms of which can be woven or knitted into textiles. The protein fiber of silk is composed mainly of fibroin (75-80%) and a smaller coating of sericin (20-25%). It is most commonly produced from the cocoons of certain insect larvae. The best-known silk is obtained from the cocoons of the larvae of the mulberry silkworm Bombyx mori, which are reared in captivity (sericulture).

about: Taktile is a financial technology company with US headquarters in New York and roots in Berlin that sells an AI-powered decision platform for banks, lenders, fintechs and insurers to automate credit and fraud decisions. It has raised about 209 million dollars. B2B with awareness among financial institutions and none among consumers.

Vecna Robotics is a US autonomous mobile robot and warehouse automation company based in Waltham, Massachusetts, selling pallet-moving robots such as autonomous tuggers and pallet jacks, plus fleet management software, to warehouses, distribution centres and manufacturers. It has raised about 214 million dollars. B2B industrial technology with no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Vecna Robotics
wiki.text: Vecna Robotics, Inc. is an American robotics and technology company headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts. Incorporated in 2018 as a spin-off from Vecna Technologies, the company specializes in automated material handling, hybrid fulfillment and workflow optimization for industrial applications.

about: CAST AI is a Kubernetes automation platform, described as US-based in Miami, Florida (with a large engineering team in Lithuania), that cuts cloud costs by automatically optimising clusters across AWS, Google Cloud and Azure. Customers are software and cloud-native companies. It has raised about 181 million dollars, including a 2025 round. B2B with developer awareness and none among consumers.

Censys is a US internet intelligence and attack surface management company based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, built on a search engine for internet-connected devices created by University of Michigan researchers. Customers are security teams, governments and large enterprises, and it has raised about 198 million dollars. B2B with awareness among cyber security professionals only.

wiki.title: Censys
wiki.text: Censys is a security service and company that provides internet intelligence based on perpetual scanning of the internet. As of 2023, it had 350,000 users. It was first created in 2015 at the University of Michigan.

about: Code Metal is a US AI company based in Boston, Massachusetts that provides a platform for translating and verifying code for embedded systems and hardware, used in defence and aerospace. It has raised about 184 million dollars. Early-stage B2B with no consumer awareness.

LiveKit is a US open-source real-time audio and video infrastructure company, based in San Jose, California, whose framework developers use to build voice and video AI applications. It powers OpenAI's ChatGPT voice mode and has raised about 181 million dollars, with a valuation above 1 billion dollars. B2B developer platform with strong awareness among developers and none among consumers.

wiki.title: LiveKit
wiki.text: LiveKit is an American technology company that provides software for building voice, video, and physical AI agents, along with cloud infrastructure. The company is based in San Francisco, California.

about: Netweb Technologies is an Indian high-performance computing and AI server maker based in Faridabad, Haryana, that designs and builds servers, workstations, storage and AI systems under its Tyrone brand for government, research and enterprise customers. It works with Nvidia and Intel, and was listed on the NSE and BSE in July 2023 (NETWEB). B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Netweb Technologies
wiki.text: Netweb Technologies India Limited is an Indian manufacturer of high-performance computing (HPC) equipment, based in Faridabad, Haryana. The company designs, builds and installs supercomputers, servers, private cloud and hyper-converged infrastructure systems, AI computing platforms and high-performance storage. Its shares are listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE).

about: Nominal is a US software company based in Los Angeles that sells a platform for testing and operating hardware systems, used by defence, aerospace and robotics firms to analyse test data. It has raised about 183 million dollars. Early-stage B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

Persefoni AI is a US climate management and carbon accounting software company based in Mesa, Arizona, helping companies, financial institutions and governments track emissions and report to regulatory standards. It has raised about 198 million dollars. B2B with awareness among sustainability teams and none among consumers.

Ultrahuman is an Indian health technology company based in Bangalore, selling the Ultrahuman Ring AIR smart ring, the M1 continuous glucose monitor app and Blood Vision tests, targeting biohacking and wellness customers in India, the US and Europe. It has raised about 185 million dollars, with exposure to a patent dispute with Oura in the US. Consumer brand with a growing following among fitness users.

wiki.title: Ultrahuman
wiki.text: Ultrahuman is a health technology company headquartered in Bengaluru, India, that designs, manufactures and sells the Ultrahuman Ring Air smart ring, the Ultrahuman M1 continuous glucose monitor, the Ultrahuman Home indoor monitoring device, and related blood testing services. Ultrahuman was incorporated in 2019 by Mohit Kumar and Vatsal Singhal. Kumar and Singhal had previously co-founded Runnr in 2015, a food delivery startup that was later acquired by Zomato.

wiki.title: Whale
wiki.what: Informal group of large marine mammals
wiki.text: Whales are a widely distributed and diverse group of fully aquatic placental marine mammals. As an informal and colloquial grouping, they correspond to large members of the infraorder Cetacea, i.e. all cetaceans apart from dolphins and porpoises. Dolphins and porpoises may be considered whales from a formal, cladistic perspective. Whales, dolphins and porpoises belong to the order Cetartiodactyla, which consists of even-toed ungulates. Their closest non-cetacean living relatives are the hippopotamuses, from which they and other cetaceans diverged about 54 million years ago. Aera Technology is a US enterprise software company based in Mountain View, California, selling a decision intelligence platform that uses AI to automate and optimise supply chain and operational decisions for large companies. It has raised about 175 million dollars including a 2023 round. B2B payments infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

Chronograph is a US software company based in Brooklyn, New York, providing portfolio monitoring, data collection and analytics tools for private equity, venture and other private capital investors. It has raised about 160 million dollars. B2B with awareness among investment firms and none among consumers.

wiki.title: Chronograph
wiki.text: A chronograph is a type of watch which is a stopwatch combined with a standard watch. A basic chronograph has hour and minute hands on the main dial to tell the time, a small seconds hand to tell that the watch is running, and a seconds hand on the main dial accompanied by a minutes sub dial for the stopwatch. Another sub dial to measure the hours of the stopwatch may also be included on a chronograph. The stopwatch can be started, stopped, and reset to zero at any time by the user by operating pushers usually placed adjacent to the crown. More complex chronographs often use additional complications and can have multiple sub-dials to measure

It serves developers and companies, and has raised about 154 million dollars. B2B with developer awareness and none among consumers.

Eclypsium is a US cybersecurity company based in Portland, Oregon, specialising in firmware, hardware and supply chain security for IT devices and infrastructure. Customers are enterprises and government agencies. It has raised about 154 million dollars. B2B with awareness among security teams and none among consumers.

HiddenLayer is a US cybersecurity company based in Austin, Texas that sells a security platform for protecting machine learning models and AI systems from attacks and theft. Customers are enterprises and government. It has raised about 156 million dollars. B2B with awareness in AI security circles and none among consumers.

Ocient is a US data analytics company based in Chicago that sells a hyperscale data warehouse for analysing very large datasets, used by telecoms, adtech and government customers. It has raised about 157 million dollars. Founded by Chris Gladwin, who earlier created Cleversafe, sold to IBM. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Chris Gladwin (engineer)
wiki.text: Chris Gladwin is an American inventor, computer engineer and technology entrepreneur, who has founded or co-founded a series of tech-related companies including MusicNow, Cleversafe and Ocient.

Prime Intellect is a US AI company based in San Francisco that builds a platform for decentralised and open-source AI training and compute, releasing open models such as INTELLECT. It has raised about 150 million dollars. Early-stage B2B with developer awareness and none among consumers.

wiki.title: Prime Intellect
wiki.text: Prime Intellect, Inc. is an American artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and computing technology company headquartered in San Francisco, California. The company develops decentralized computing software designed to aggregate distributed GPU infrastructure, enabling multi-node training, reinforcement learning (RL), and autonomous agent execution over the internet.

about: Black Forest Labs is a German AI start-up from Freiburg im Breisgau, founded in 2024 by creators of Stable Diffusion, building generative image models such as the FLUX series, and offering them via API and open weights. Customers include developers and companies. It raised large funding, with more than $450 million shown. B2B AI lab with strong profile among creators.

wiki.title: Flux (text-to-image model)
wiki.text: Flux is a family of text-to-image and image-to-image models developed by Black Forest Labs (BFL), based in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany. Black Forest Labs was founded by former employees of Stability AI. As with other text-to-image models, Flux generates images from natural language descriptions, called prompts. In addition, some Flux models support editing images.

about: Fiture is a Chinese smart home fitness company, based in Chengdu, Sichuan, selling interactive fitness mirrors and AI-driven workout equipment with subscription classes. Founded in 2019, it raised around $390 million. Customers are consumers. Chinese consumer fitness brand with modest awareness outside China.
cb_desc: Fiture is a smart household fitness equipment brand.

about: Mysten Labs is a US blockchain company based in Palo Alto, California, founded in 2021 by former Meta Diem engineers, that builds the Sui layer-1 network and Walrus storage tooling for web3 applications. It raised about $336 million from a16z, Binance Labs and others. B2B crypto infrastructure with an active sponsorship interest.

Sitecore is a digital experience platform and customer experience management software company. Its products cover web content management, personalization, commerce, customer data and marketing automation for large enterprises. Founded in Denmark in 2001 and now with executive offices in the US, it is backed by EQT since 2016 and serves thousands of customers worldwide. Funding shown suggests private equity financing, with EQT as the lead owner. B2B enterprise software brand with limited consumer visibility.

about: Vivint is a US smart home technology company selling professionally installed security systems, cameras, doorbell cameras, automation and solar energy services under subscription contracts, through direct-to-home sales teams. It was founded in 1999 (as APX Alarm) and headquartered in Lehi, Utah. Blackstone acquired it in 2012, it listed through a SPAC in 2020 as Vivint Smart Home (NYSE: VVNT), and in 2023 NRG Energy acquired it for roughly 2.8 billion dollars. It serves about two million subscribers. Recognized US consumer brand, known for stadium naming partnerships such as the Utah Jazz arena.

wiki.title: Vivint
wiki.text: Vivint Smart Home, Inc. is a Provo, Utah-based manufacturer of smart home and home security products. Its product lines include cameras, locks, safety sensors, thermostats, and lighting, along with associated monitoring and installation services. The company is a subsidiary of NRG Energy, which acquired Vivint in 2022 for $2.8 billion.

about: Cloudera is a data management and analytics software company, born from the Hadoop era. Its platform lets enterprises store, process and analyse data across clouds and data centres, with offerings for machine learning, data engineering and data warehousing, and it merged with Hortonworks in 2019. Headquartered in Santa Clara, California, it listed on the NYSE in 2017 and was taken private by KKR and Clayton, Dubilier & Rice in 2021 in a roughly 5.3 billion dollar deal. B2B enterprise software with no consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Cloudera

wiki.title: E2open
wiki.text: E2open Parent Holdings, Inc. was founded as a business-to-business provider of cloud-based, on-demand software for supply chains for computer, telecom and electronics systems, components and services. The company was founded in 2000 as a joint project of 8 major companies: Hitachi, IBM, LG Electronics, Matsushita, Nortel, Seagate, Solectron, and Toshiba.

about: Tanium is an endpoint management and security software company that gives IT and security teams real-time visibility and control of laptops, servers and devices on large networks, with products for asset discovery, patching, risk and compliance. Founded by David Hindawi and Orion Hindawi, it is headquartered in Kirkland/Bellevue, Washington, privately held and valued at around 9 billion dollars in 2020. Customers include large enterprises and government agencies, with funding of about 1 billion dollars. B2B cybersecurity brand with limited public consumer recognition.

wiki.title: Tanium

wiki.text: Tanium is a privately held cybersecurity and systems management company founded in 2007 with headquarters in Kirkland, Washington, and its operations center in Emeryville, California.

about: Avaya is an enterprise communications company providing unified communications, contact centre software and cloud collaboration tools such as Avaya Experience Platform, serving large organisations, governments and call centres in over 100 countries. It was formed from Lucent's enterprise business in 2000, headquartered in Morristown, New Jersey (later Durham, NC), listed on the NYSE, and went through Chapter 11 bankruptcies in 2017 and 2023. It had about 5,000 employees post-restructuring. B2B brand with legacy telephone recognition; also a past sports sponsor.

about: Dataiku is an enterprise AI and data science platform that lets analysts, data scientists and engineers build, deploy and govern machine learning and generative AI applications. Founded in Paris in 2013 and now headquartered in New York, it serves large companies in banking, retail, pharma and manufacturing with subscription software. Backed by Tiger Global, Insight, CapitalG, and Snowflake Ventures, it was valued at around 3.7 billion dollars in 2022. B2B software with low consumer awareness; strong among data practitioners.

wiki.title: Dataiku
wiki.text: Dataiku is a French-American artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning company which was founded in 2013 in Paris, France. In December 2019, Dataiku announced that CapitalG—the late-stage growth venture capital fund financed by Alphabet Inc.—joined Dataiku as an investor and that it had achieved unicorn status. As of 2021, Dataiku is valued at $4.6 billion. As of 2022, the company employs more than 1,000 people worldwide between offices in New York, Denver, Washington DC, Los Angeles, Paris, London, Munich, Frankfurt, Sydney, Singapore, Tokyo, and Dubai.

about: EcoVadis is a French company that provides business sustainability ratings, assessing suppliers' environmental, social and ethical performance through its collaborative platform. Corporations use it to evaluate supply chains, and suppliers pay to be rated and use its medals. Founded in 2007 in Paris, it has hundreds of thousands of rated companies and large customers such as Johnson & Johnson and Coca-Cola. It raised funding from General Atlantic, Partners Group and CVC, with a valuation of over 1 billion dollars. B2B with low consumer visibility.

OutSystems is a low-code application development platform that lets enterprises build, deploy and manage web and mobile applications quickly, with AI-assisted development tools. It sells subscriptions to large organisations in financial services, insurance, healthcare, government and retail, with several thousand customers worldwide. Founded in Portugal in 2001 and now headquartered in Boston, it is backed by KKR and Tiger Global (valued at around 9.5 billion dollars in 2021) and has well over 1,000 employees. B2B software with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: OutSystems

about: Arqiva is a UK communications infrastructure and media services company. It owns and operates the national terrestrial TV and radio broadcast transmission network, thousands of towers and masts, and is a major provider of smart metering communications and satellite and media services. Customers include broadcasters, mobile operators and utilities. It is headquartered near Winchester, Hampshire, and has been owned by a consortium including Macquarie, IFM and Ontario Teachers' pension plan. B2B infrastructure brand with moderate recognition in the UK media sector.

wiki.title: Arqiva
wiki.what: British telecommunications and broadcast infrastructure company
wiki.text: Arqiva is a British telecommunications company which provides infrastructure, broadcast transmission and smart meter facilities in the United Kingdom. The company is headquartered at the former Independent Broadcasting Authority headquarters in Crawley, Hampshire, England. Its main customers are broadcasters and utility companies, and its main asset is a network of around 1,500 radio and television transmission sites. It is owned by a consortium of investors led by Digital 9 Infrastructure and the Australian investment house Macquarie Bank. Arqiva is a patron of the Radio Academy.

about: Collibra is a data intelligence and governance software company, offering a platform for data catalogues, data quality and privacy compliance used by large enterprises in finance, pharma and government. Founded in 2008 in Brussels, it is now headquartered in New York, with a valuation of 5.25 billion dollars after its 2021 funding round led by ICONIQ, Index Ventures and Tiger Global. B2B software with no consumer visibility.

Skillsoft is a corporate learning and talent development company providing online courses, books, videos, coaching and AI-powered skill assessments to businesses and governments. It owns Global Knowledge training and Codecademy, and was combined with Churchill Capital Corp II in a 2021 SPAC deal; listed on the NYSE (SKIL). Based in Nashua, New Hampshire, with tens of thousands of enterprise customers and around 2,000 employees. B2B learning provider, widely known among HR and L&D teams, little consumer visibility outside Codecademy.

wiki.title: Skillsoft
wiki.text: Skillsoft is an American educational technology company that produces learning management system software and content.

about: 6sense is a B2B revenue marketing and sales intelligence platform that uses AI and intent data to identify accounts that are in the market to buy and to orchestrate account-based marketing. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in San Francisco, it counts several thousand enterprise customers, and was valued at 5.2 billion dollars in 2021, backed by Sapphire Ventures, Insight Partners, Tiger Global and others. B2B software brand, well known among marketers, no consumer awareness.

Cyxtera Technologies was a data centre and colocation operator, spun out of CenturyLink's assets in 2017 and owned by BC Partners, with about 60 facilities worldwide and the Cyxtera Cyber fabric. It listed through a SPAC with Starboard Value Acquisition Corp. in 2021 (Nasdaq: CYXT). It filed for Chapter 11 in June 2023, and its assets were largely acquired by Brookfield Infrastructure in 2023. Based in Coppell, Texas, previously Coral Gables, Florida. B2B infrastructure with limited public awareness.

Edgio was a content delivery network and edge cloud company formed in 2022 when Limelight Networks acquired Edgecast (from Apollo) and rebranded. It served video streaming, web security and application acceleration to media and software customers. Based in Phoenix, Arizona, it listed on Nasdaq (EGIO) but struggled with debt and weak revenue, filed for Chapter 11 in September 2024, and its assets were sold, partly to Akamai. B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Edgio
wiki.text: Edgio, Inc., formerly Limelight Networks, was an American company that provided a content delivery network (CDN) service used for delivery of digital media content and software.

about: NEAR is a blockchain protocol and platform developed by the NEAR Foundation and Near Inc., designed for scalable decentralised applications and AI agents, with a sharded proof-of-stake network and the NEAR token. It was founded in 2018 by Illia Polosukhin and Alexander Skidanov, who had worked in machine learning, and is based in San Francisco, with backers including a16z, Pantera and Tiger Global. Funding of about 534 million dollars. Known in the crypto community; consumer awareness is limited.

wiki.title: NEAR Shoemaker
wiki.text: Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous (NEAR), later renamed NEAR Shoemaker in honor of planetary scientist Eugene Shoemaker, was a robotic space probe developed by the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory for NASA. Launched in 1996, it was designed to study the near-Earth asteroid 433 Eros from orbit over the course of a year. It was the first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid and successfully land on one. In February 2000, NEAR Shoemaker reached Eros and entered orbit around it. On February 12, 2001, the spacecraft landed on the asteroid and was deactivated just over two weeks later.

about: PagerDuty is a San Francisco-based digital operations management platform that alerts engineering teams about incidents, coordinates response and automates workflows, with AI features, used by thousands of companies including large enterprises. Founded in 2009, it listed on the NYSE in 2019 (PD), with revenue near 450 million dollars. Customers pay subscriptions. B2B developer tool brand with strong recognition among software and IT operations teams, none among general consumers.

wiki.title: PagerDuty
wiki.text: PagerDuty, Inc. is an American cloud computing company specializing in a SaaS incident management platform for IT operations departments.

about: AEye is a Pleasanton, California lidar company that develops adaptive, high-performance lidar systems for automotive, trucking and industrial applications, for example the Apollo and 4Sight products, using software-defined scanning. It listed on Nasdaq through a SPAC with CF Finance Acquisition Corp. III in 2021 (LIDR), and shifted to licensing and an industrial focus in later years. Funding of around 364 million dollars. B2B sensor supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Chronosphere is a cloud-native observability platform headquartered in New York that helps engineering teams monitor and control metrics, traces and logs and cost of data. Founded in 2019 by former Uber engineers Martin Mao and Rob Skillington, it serves large companies such as DoorDash, Snap and Robinhood, and was valued at about 1.6 billion dollars in 2022. In late 2025, Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire it for about 3.35 billion dollars. B2B software with no consumer visibility.

CoachHub is a Berlin-based digital coaching platform founded in 2018 by Matti Niebelschuetz and Yannis Niebelschuetz, offering corporate employees access to certified coaches by video and an AI coaching assistant, AIMY. It serves large enterprises across more than 70 countries and over 3,500 coaches, and was valued at about 1 billion dollars after Series C in 2022 backed by Highland Europe and Partech. B2B HR tech brand.

Preferred Networks is a Tokyo-based artificial intelligence company, founded in 2014 by Toru Nishikawa and Daisuke Okanohara, that works on deep learning for manufacturing, robotics, drug discovery and its own AI chips (MN-Core), and operates supercomputers. It built the Chainer framework. Investors include Toyota, NTT, Fanuc and Mitsui. Customers include industrial firms and automakers. Funding is shown in yen (44.6 billion). B2B brand known among AI researchers, not consumers.

wiki.title: Preferred Networks
wiki.text: Preferred Networks Inc. is a Japanese startup focused on the research and development of deep learning for IoT applications. The company was spun off from Preferred Infrastructure (PFI), founded by Toru Nishikawa, Daisuke Okanohara, and others on March 26, 2014.

about: Sayari Labs (Sayari) is a Washington, DC, provider of corporate and trade risk intelligence, data and graph analytics, mapping company ownership, supply chains and sanctions exposure for banks, governments and compliance teams. Founded in 2015, it sells subscriptions to financial institutions, government agencies and corporates. Funding of about 330 million dollars is shown. B2B and government data brand with a niche profile.

about: Zip is a San Francisco procurement orchestration platform that helps companies handle intake, approvals, sourcing, purchasing and payments for business spend, with AI agents. Founded in 2020 by Rujul Zaparde and Lu Cheng, it is used by large enterprises such as OpenAI, Snowflake and Reddit, and was valued around 2.2 billion dollars in 2024, backed by Y Combinator, Tiger Global and BOND. B2B software, strong in finance and procurement circles.

Writer is a San Francisco enterprise generative AI company offering a full-stack platform, including its own Palmyra language models, an agent builder and guardrails, for companies to automate marketing, HR and operations work. Founded in 2020 by May Habib and Waseem Alshikh, it counts customers such as Uber, Vanguard and Intuit, and was valued at around 1.9 billion dollars in 2024, backed by Iconiq, Radical Ventures, Premji Invest and others. B2B software brand with little consumer recognition.

wiki.title: Writer
wiki.text: A writer is a person who uses written words to communicate ideas, to inspire feelings and emotions, or to entertain. They use various writing styles, genres, and techniques, and may write novels, short stories, monographs, travelogues, plays, screenplays, teleplays, songs, and essays as well as reports, educational material, and news articles that may be of interest to the general public. Writers' works are nowadays published in a wide range of media. Skilled writers who are able to use language to express ideas well often contribute significantly to the cultural content of a society.

about: Altana is a New York company building a global supply chain intelligence network, the Altana Atlas, which uses AI and data sharing to map trade flows for customs authorities, logistics firms and manufacturers, for compliance and risk. Founded in 2018 by Evan Smith, it counts government agencies and large companies as customers, and has been valued at around 1 billion dollars after funding from Insight, Salesforce Ventures and Thomas H. Lee-like investors. B2B and government brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Altana
wiki.text: Altana AG is a German chemical company headquartered in Wesel. It was created in 1977, as a result of spinning off divisions from the Varta Group. The first CEO was Herbert Quandt.

about: Aqua Security is a cloud native security company founded in Israel in 2015 and now headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts, selling a platform that protects containers, Kubernetes, serverless and cloud workloads from build to runtime, and the open-source scanner Trivy. Customers are large enterprises and financial institutions. Backed by M12, Lightspeed, Insight and others, with about 325 million dollars raised. B2B developer security brand, with no consumer awareness.

Avathon is a Pleasanton, California AI technology company, which grew from SparkCognition (rebranded in 2024/2025), providing industrial AI for predictive maintenance, grid and asset monitoring, and autonomy to energy, manufacturing and defence customers. SparkCognition was founded in 2013 in Austin by Amir Husain. Funding of around 287 million dollars is shown. B2B industrial software with no consumer brand visibility.

about: BigID is a New York data intelligence and privacy software company that discovers, classifies and governs sensitive data across cloud and on-premises systems using machine learning, helping firms with compliance such as GDPR and CCPA. Founded in 2016 by Dimitri Sirota and Nimrod Vax, it has customers among large enterprises and has been valued at roughly 1 billion dollars, with investors including Tiger Global, Bessemer and Advent. B2B software brand, with strong recognition in data privacy circles.

Corelight is a San Francisco cybersecurity company selling network detection and response built on the open-source Zeek network monitoring framework, used for threat hunting by security teams in large organisations, governments and research. Founded in 2013 by the Zeek creators Vern Paxson, Robin Sommer and Greg Bell, it raised around 309 million dollars from General Catalyst, Accel and Capital One Ventures. B2B security brand known in technical circles, with no consumer awareness.

Huntress is a Columbia, Maryland cybersecurity company that provides managed endpoint detection and response, identity and security awareness services, aimed at small and mid-sized businesses through managed service providers. Founded in 2015 by former NSA operators, it protects millions of endpoints and raised about 310 million dollars from Sixth Street, Georgian and Insight. B2B security brand well known among IT service providers, and little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Huntress (company)
wiki.text: Huntress is an American cybersecurity company based in Columbia, Maryland.

about: Iru (formerly Kandji) is an AI-powered security and IT management platform for Apple devices and wider endpoint fleets, used by companies to manage and secure Macs, iPhones and other devices. Founded in 2018 and based in San Diego, it appears in the input with a Miami location after a 2025 rebrand. It is backed by Greylock, Tiger Global and General Catalyst and has about 288 million dollars of funding. B2B software with strong recognition in IT circles.
cb_desc: Iru is the Al-powered security & IT platform used by the world.

wiki.title: Iru (company)
wiki.text: Iru, formerly known as Kandji, is an American technology company that develops an enterprise device management and security platform. It is based in San Francisco, California.

about: OG is a San Francisco technology startup and foundation described as developing a web3 and AI platform, with funding of about 325 million dollars shown. The input does not provide details on its products, customers or backers. The name matches several possible entities. B2B or crypto infrastructure with no known consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Tractian is an industrial AI company, founded in Brazil in 2019 by Igor Marinelli and Gabriel Lameirinhas and now headquartered in Atlanta, offering sensors and software for predictive maintenance and monitoring of machinery in factories, with AI analytics. Customers include large manufacturers in the Americas. It raised about 314 million dollars from Sequoia, General Catalyst and Next47, and was valued above 1 billion dollars. B2B industrial technology brand with little consumer awareness.

Hex Technologies is a San Francisco data science and analytics platform that lets teams build collaborative notebooks, apps and AI-assisted analysis in a shared workspace. Founded in 2019 by Barry McCardel, Caitlin Colgrove and Glen Takahashi, it counts customers such as Anthropic, Reddit and Notion, and has raised more than 100 million dollars from Andreessen Horowitz, Snowflake Ventures and others. The input is garbled by an OCR error, and a funding of 271 million dollars is shown. B2B software brand known among data teams.

about: Avalanche is a layer-1 blockchain platform for smart contracts and custom networks, built by Ava Labs, which was founded in 2018 by Emin Gun Sirer and is based in New York. Its AVAX token is traded on exchanges, and the network is used for decentralised finance, gaming and tokenised real-world assets. Funding of about 270 million dollars is shown, including a token sale in 2021. Known in crypto circles, with a record of marketing partnerships and sports sponsorships; little general consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Avalanche
wiki.what: Rapid flow of a mass of snow down a slope
wiki.text: An avalanche is a rapid flow of snow down a slope, such as a hill or mountain. Avalanches can be triggered spontaneously, by factors such as increased precipitation or snowpack weakening, or by external means such as humans, other animals, and earthquakes. Primarily composed of flowing snow and air, large avalanches have the capability to capture and move ice, rocks, and trees.

about: ChapsVision is a French software group based in Suresnes, near Paris, offering data, AI, cyber and analytics software for governments, security, defence, finance and retail, created through acquisitions such as Sinequa and Bluenove. It was founded in 2019 by Olivier Dellenbach and backed by Eurazeo and Weinberg Capital Partners among others. Funding is about 275 million. B2B and government software with little consumer brand awareness.
